title: V'Tar
text: This is the raw, unaltered power of the plane from Voltari. They have countless uses, including repairing the V'Torrak to achieve the Supremacy victory. If one plays the Supremacy, one wins by collecting a certain amount of V'Tar, as determined from the respective arena in which one is playing.

title: V'Tar orb
text:
the V'Tar Orbs are the key to powering the ancient V'Torrak artifact. In the Supremacy scenario, mages fight around the controller of these balls. The V’Tar Orbs are summon items that are located in different zones of the arena at the start of a Domination game. Controller over these balls is the key to victory!
The balls are represented through double-sided tokens. a side of the marker shows the ball in the “Off” condition. All V’Tar balls start the game in this condition, which they have been in for centuries! the first melee attack they hit turns them “a”; To do this, one turns the token onto its “a” side.
The balls start the game “neutral”, no player controls them. During the game, the players will try to grab the controller over a ball. If you control a sphere, mark it with a colored control marker. Balls are controlled by the magician whose marker color is on them. Balls without token are “neutral”.
Balls cannot be destroyed. one can attack them, but one does not inflict any damage on them.

title: V'Torrak artifact
text:
This zone contains a long-standing V'Torrak artifact that can break down the boundaries between worlds and provide its controller with almost infinite mana. If you control this zone (see zone control), you may summon a Sslak to this zone during the deployment phase. To summon the Sslak, you must pay its mana cost and spend a V’Tar to take the spell card from outside your spell book. like every other creature summoned by you, the Sslak is under your controller.
Note: if this zone part should lose its special ability (perhaps because a terrain spell replaces its effect), applies the V'Torrak artifact then as "buried under this zone" and the player who collects enough V'Tar still wins the game. thus in arenas without the V'Torrak one can win a scenario "the Supremacy".
Placement tip: the V'Torrak works well if you place it near zones with V'Tar orbs. This allows you to use it to summon Sslak, which is used to guard the orbs. It should do well in the center of the arena, or at least within equal distance to all starting zones or zones with V’Tar bullets. If you place a V’Tar Orb here, you should thus give the zone an additional guard.

text: The #linked table to attack sequence shows the different types of attacks in Mage Wars and their exact sequence. title: attack action
text:
an attack action is a quick or full creature action to make an attack. Sometimes the attack action is an individual attack, sometimes it consists of multiple attacks. Double strike, triple strike or a sweeping are an attack action, but consist of several attacks. a zone attack is a single attack action that performs an individual attack against each object in a zone.
Some attacks, like counterstrike, attacks from walls or conjurations do not consume their own action. In these cases, the attacks are counted as their own attack action, so spells that refer to an attack action apply here. an overview of the sequence of the attack action gives the linked table to attack sequence.

title: attack spell

If you use an attack spell, this is both a spell, as thus an attack. Therefore you must like common magic, first follow all steps for the use. If the spell is not countered, you then carry out the attack by following the attack steps. The target of the attack is automatically the target you chose to use your spell. attack spells have no symbol for quick or full action in their attack stat line, because the respective action is already carried out when the spell is used. Thus the range of the attack corresponds to that of the spell, therefore the range information is missing in the attack stat line. There is therefore no attack name, because it corresponds to the name of the spell.

title: condition
text:
Objects can take on different conditions that are displayed with tokens that are placed on the object. all conditions can accumulate and their effects increase accordingly. spell and attacks can cause a whole range of effects and conditions in addition to (or instead of from) damage.
an effect is a short, instantaneous change to the target's status. one does not require any game material, around a effect to mark. For example, the target could be bumped into an adjacent zone.
a condition lasts longer and will be marked with a token on the target. Condition tokens are printed on both sides, after which the side that shows the condition valid for the target object must always be on top. For example, if the target burns, there is a token burn on it.
all conditions can thus lie multiple times on the same object. This could increase their effect. For example, a creature with two Condition Token weak would receive a penalty from 2 on all of its attacks without spell. However, some conditions can be made worse by this. For example, a creature with the condition stun cannot perform any actions until the end of its next action phase. If they received another token stun, they would only continue to be incapacitated until the end of their next action phase, not longer.
most conditions can be removed in a certain way. Some conditions are automatically removed, for others one requires an escape roll. Saving throws are always executed at the end of the action phase of a creature. one throws the effect the: if the result corresponds to the numbers on the token, this will be taken away. otherwise it remains on the creature until the end of its next action phase, in which a new escape roll can be attempted.

title: damage barrier
text:
a damage barrier surrounds an object and performs an automatic attack against any enemy that attacks an object in the melee that is surrounded by such a barrier.

This attack takes place automatically in step 8: damage barrier instead of. if at least a melee attack has successfully hit the defender, he must attack with the damage barrier.

To attack they only need the two steps 3: roll dice and 4: damage and effects. they trigger no further damage barrier attacks or a counterstrike.

Effects, spell and conditions that modify a creature's attacks, including stun, sleep, daze, weak, etc. have no effect on damage barriers. the damage barrier will thus be used when the defender has been destroyed through the attack. traits the defending creature (which will be attacked from the damage barrier) can modify the damage barrier attack, such as aegis 1 or a suitable damage type modifier, like flame +2.

text:
Objects with the trait spawn point have the property that they can use spell for you. example: the Beastmaster has a Dwelling with channeling 2. in each channeling phase he places 2 Mana tokens on the Dwelling. title: spellbind
text:
spellbind is a trait that some objects possess (mostly equipment spell). This trait allowed you to attach a spell to the object.
If you apply a spell with the trait spellbind, you immediately bind a spell to it. you can choose any spell from your spellbook that meets the restrictions of the spellbind object. For example, the Mage Wand may only bind an incantation to itself, so you cannot attach an attack spell or an enchantment to it. Place the bound spell face down under the spell binding object. the bound spell can be cast like a spell that you prepared in the planning phase. you can only use it once per round. When you use the bound spell, uncover it and show it to your enemy. From then on it remains uncovered and partially visible under the object to which it is bound. To use the spell you must use the required action, pay the full mana cost and as usual range, target and LOS check.
Bound formulas or attack spell are not discarded after use. The spellbinding object retains this spell so you can use it again and again in future rounds. thus if This spell is countered, it will also not be discarded and remains bound. If the spell binding object will be destroyed, the spell bound to it will also be destroyed. If an equipment spell with spellbind returns to your spellbook (e.g. because it was replaced by another equipment), a spell bound to it returns to the book.
Some spellbind items allow you to exchange the spell bound to it for another. the old spell comes back into your spellbook.
example: you can bind any incantation to the magician's wand. you bind a weak heal to it. As long as the Wand remains in play, you can use the spell Weak Heal once per round, as whether you had prepared it each time in the planning phase. If a spell with the trait spellbind cast or a bound spell wants to be replaced, you take the bound spell from your mage's spellbook and not a the spell selected in the planning phase. If a mage uses an equipment with spellbind on another mage, the other mage selects the bound spell from his spellbook. if a bound spell is countered, only the effect is countered, the spell itself remains bound (it will neither be destroyed nor discarded). the applies thus, if the spell fails or becomes ineffective (e.g. through Hex), or if the target changes or moves. If you steal an item with a bound spell (e.g. steal through enchantment), you thus steal the bound spell. If This spell is still face down, you can now look at it. As controller, your mage may use this spell as long as it is not forbidden due to an enemy school. If the bound spell is exchanged, it returns to the owner's spellbook.

title: spellbook
text:
When you create your spellbook, you will spend your magician's spell points to purchase your desired spell cards. you may not spend more spell points than your maximum on your mage-property card. Each spell in Mage Wars has a spell level. This value roughly corresponds to the power of the spell and the difficulty of using it. Each spell also belongs to one of the schools of magic. The number of spell points you must spend to add a spell to your book depends on the spell level and the magic schools in which your mage was trained.
If you want to put a spell at a school in which your mage was trained in your spellbook, you must pay spell points equal to the level of that spell. If you take a spell from a school in which your mage is not trained, you must pay spell points equal to twice the level of that spell.
Some mages are enemies of certain schools. These schools are listed on your property card under the training section. For example, the warlock must pay three times the number of spell points to be able to put a holy spell in his spellbook. Since each spell can only be used once during the game, you will definitely want to have several copies of important spells. you can have up to 6 copies of each spell with level 1 and up to 4 copies of spells major level. from each epic spell you may have at most 1 edition in your spellbook. Novice spells are relatively simple spells with low mana costs and limited effects that can still be useful for a mage. Each mage can buy any novice spell for 1 magic point each, regardless of the school. from each epic spell you may have at most 1 edition in your spellbook.

title: training
text:
Your mage is trained in one or more schools of magic. These are the spells that are easiest for your mage to cast. If you want to put a spell from a school in which your mage was trained in your spellbook, you must pay spell points equal to the level of that spell.
If you take a spell from a school in which your mage was not trained, you must pay spell points equal to twice the level of that spell.
Some spells belong to more than a magical school. spells that belong to multiple schools (an “or” connects these schools on the card) allow you to choose which school you choose for such a spell. Your spell level is the level specified for all these schools. For example, the Elemental Wand is a spell with level 2, and either Fire, Earth, water or Air. the Warlock trained in fire magic can thus treat him as a fire spell and add 2 spell points to his spellbook.

For example, Adramelech is both a Fire spell, level 2, and thus a Dark spell, level 4. thus Adramelech counts as a spell level 6 (2 Fire + 4 Dark). The wizard trained in Fire Magic, but not Dark Magic, would have to pay 10 spell points to put this demon in his spellbook [2 Fire + (4 x 2) Dark]. The Warlock, who is trained both in Dark Magic and Fire Magic, only pays 6 points for it.

He must pay three times the cost for fire spells (which is listed in the training section of his card). You would have to pay 9 spell points to buy a fire spell, level 3.
